item.title: Surviving empire
item.description: Everything is coming apart at the seams. Once long-held assumptions about the international order no longer apply. Today the very idea of international law has been pushed aside in favor of naked aggression. Treaty alliances don’t count for much. Even worse, many elites no longer fear war. CrossTalking with Daniel McAdams, Jenin Younes, and Tyler Nixon.

item.title: Energy shock
item.description: The energy shock the entire world is experiencing is not going away anytime soon. What happens if the Persian Gulf does not stay there? How is this energy shock different from the past and have the international energy markets been forever changed? CrossTalking with Michael Hudson and Radhika Desai.

item.title: CrossTalk Bullhorns: Start of endgame
item.description: With Ukraine on the ropes and its infrastructure being destroyed, the American administration makes an energy deal with Russia. Meanwhile, NATO brass gather in Kiev to access the damage they have brought about. Also, can the Mecca defense alliance save the House of Saud? Is a new order coming in the Middle East? CrossTalking with George Szamuely and Mark Sleboda.

item.title: CrossTalk Bullhorns: Between war and peace
item.description: Neither war nor peace – this is where the Iran war stands at the moment. Is this a pause and prelude to the next stage of kinetic warfare? After the midterms? Also, Russia’s Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad is in focus. Strangely, the West is outraged that Russia will defend its sovereignty at all costs. CrossTalking with George Szamuely and Mark Sleboda.

item.title: The great unraveling
item.description: We are witnessing a great unraveling of the global order. Western, particularly American, hegemony is coming apart at the seams. Is the future greater multipolarity? We can only hope so. However, hegemony is never surrendered easily or willingly. Change is fraught with danger and more violence. CrossTalking with Michael Rossi, Alexis Poulin, and Ali Borhani.

item.title: CrossTalk Bullhorns: Rejecting peace (again)
item.description: At this year’s United Nations General Assembly gathering Iran proposed a seven-day roadmap to end the war. Donald Trump was quick to reply. He said, “I reject their proposal.” Is this yet another missed opportunity to achieve peace? Also, why is Europe so desperate for a war against Russia that it can’t win? CrossTalking with Tarik Cyril Amar and Aleksandar Pavic.
